title: TPA raises land rights, resettlement issues with Australian High Commissioner
byline: A delegation of the Tamil Progressive Alliance (TPA), led by its leader and Member of Parliament Mano Ganesan, met Australian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka Matthew Duckworth in Colombo on Thursday to discuss issues affecting the Malaiyaha Tamil community, including land rights, disaster resettlement, and inclusive national development.

title: Trump unveils Qatari luxury jet for Air Force One fleet
byline: President Donald Trump has unveiled a new Boeing 747-8 jet for Air Force One that the Qatari government donated last year as an ’’unconditional’’ gift to the US.

title: Court dismisses Daya Group’s writ application against People’s Bank auction
byline: The Court of Appeal dismissed a writ application filed by Daya Group Limited and Daya Apparel Export (Pvt) Ltd challenging the People’s Bank’s move to auction mortgaged properties under its parate execution powers, holding that the bank was legally entitled to proceed with the recovery process.

title: Dominican national nabbed with Hashish worth over Rs. 375Mn
byline: A 24-year-old Dominican national has been arrested at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) for allegedly attempting to smuggle a large stock of Hashish into the country.

title: Showers expected in several provinces
byline: Several spells of showers are expected in the Western, Sabaragamuwa and North-Western provinces, as well as in the Galle, Matara, Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts, according to the Department of Meteorology.

title: Netanyahu actions may undermine Trump-Iran peace deal, US intelligence warns
byline: US intelligence agencies have warned the Trump administration that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is likely to take steps that could undermine Washington’s efforts to secure a lasting peace agreement with Iran, according to a report by The Washington Post.

title: Over 225,000 students qualify for A/Ls
byline: A total of 225,748 students who sat the 2025 G.C.E. Ordinary Level Examination have qualified for the G.C.E. Advanced Level Examination, Commissioner General of Examinations Indika Kumari Liyanage announced.

title: Special security and traffic plan for Poson season
byline: The Sri Lanka Police has announced a comprehensive island-wide security and traffic management plan in preparation for the upcoming Poson festival. This year’s Poson Full Moon Poya Day falls on June 29, 2026, and is expected to attract large numbers of devotees to religious sites across the country.

title: Australia confirms first case of H5N1 bird flu as virus reaches every continent
byline: The H5N1 strain of bird flu has for the first time been found in Australia, the country’s agriculture ministry confirmed. It means the highly contagious variant has now reached every continent.

title: India ready for work once Sri Lanka green-lights project
byline: India remains ready to initiate steps regarding the land connectivity project between the two countries once Sri Lanka gives the go-ahead, according to a top source familiar with the subject.

title: UNFPA facilitate mental health enhancement and psychosocial support for frontline responders of Ditwah
byline: United Nations Populations Fund (UNFPA) has embarked on a mission to facilitate mental health enhancement and psychosocial support for frontline responders of Ditwah and other state workers.

title: Court dismisses Daya Group’s writ application against People’s Bank auction
byline: The Court of Appeal yesterday dismissed a writ application filed by Daya Group Limited and Daya Apparel Export (Pvt) Ltd challenging People’s Bank’s move to auction mortgaged properties under its parate execution powers, holding that the bank was legally entitled to proceed with the recovery process.

title: Govt. to repeal PTA, introduce new law within two months: Minister
byline: The Government intends to repeal the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) and introduce a new people-centric piece of legislation within the next two months, Minister of Justice and National Integration Harshana Nanayakkara said.

title: Principal, Vice Principal arrested over concealing sexual abuse of a schoolgirl by a schoolboy
byline: The Principal, the Vice Principal of Ambalantota Therapuththa National School and a schoolboy of another school were arrested yesterday in connection with the grave sexual abuse of a schoolgirl during the sports meet of the school on May 21.

title: IMF urged not to insist on removal of subsidies on fuel
byline: A delegation of the Joint Opposition has requested the International Monetary Fund (IMF) representative in Sri Lanka not to insist on the removal of fuel subsidies, as it would inflict unbearable hardship on the people at this time.

title: Three-month concession given for vehicles without seatbelts
byline: The National Council for Road Safety said that  a final three-month grace period will be given for owners of vehicles that were originally manufactured without seatbelts to install the required safety equipment.

title: Pakistan cuts petrol price by Rs74 after US-Iran peace deal eases oil costs
byline: Pakistan on Friday slashed fuel prices by up to Rs74 per liter after a peace agreement between the United States and Iran helped ease pressure on global oil markets, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif saying the government was passing on the full benefit of lower international prices to consumers.

title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz over ceasefire violations - MEHR
byline: Iran’s top joint military command, ​Khatam al-Anbiya Central ‌Headquarters, said on Saturday that the Strait ​of Hormuz would ​be closed to vessel ⁠traffic, citing ​alleged violations of a ​ceasefire agreement by the U.S. and Israel, Iran’s ​Mehr state ​news agency reported.

title: Final weekend to see Dehiwala Zoo’s lion cubs up close
byline: The special opportunity for visitors to see the two lion cubs born at the Dehiwala Zoological Gardens from close range will end on Sunday (June 21), with the Department of National Zoological Gardens urging the public to make the most of the final weekend.

title: At least seven killed in twin roadside bombings in northwest Pakistan
byline: Two roadside bombs in restive northwestern Pakistan killed at least seven people on Saturday, authorities said.

title: Seat belt law comes into force across Sri Lanka from today
byline: The National Council for Road Safety announced that the mandatory enforcement of Sri Lanka’s seat belt law comes into effect from today (20), following the conclusion of the grace period granted for motorists.

title: Australia vows to rein in any H5N1 birdflu after confirming first case
byline: Australia will do all it can to curb any spread of H5N1 bird flu, Prime Minister Anthony ​Albanese said on Saturday, as the first mainland infection was confirmed ‌in a seabird a day after being detected in a remote southwestern region.

title: Suspect arrested in Meetiyagoda with over 1kg of ICE
byline: A 32-year-old man was arrested in the Iranawila area of Meetiyagoda after police recovered more than one kilogram of the narcotic known as “ICE” and 750 grams of heroin during a raid conducted by the Central Crime Investigation Bureau (CCIB).

title: Fuel price relief possible by August or September if global prices remain stable: Bimal
byline: The government could pass on the benefits of lower global fuel prices to the public by August or September, provided international fuel prices remain at their current levels, Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development Bimal Rathnayake said.
